name: milnor-tiling-certificate-probe
description: Certificate probe for H4-5c-ii(b): every algebraic fact the Lean tiling proof rests on -- the two subset identities, the sign relation and the all-same-sign exclusion it buys, the vertex incidence anchoring the triangle's definition, and the set-level tiling itself.

assertions.name: subset_identity_next_residual
assertions.detail: cos(psi)F = sin(psi+psi')G2 + cos(psi')G3, next orientation (Lean: wedgeAt_lt_chord_next)

assertions.name: all_same_sign_violations
assertions.detail: the relation forbids (+,+,+) and (-,-,-); this is the covering argument (Lean: inscribedTriangle_subset_milnorWedges_of_ne)

assertions.name: vertex_on_line_residual
assertions.detail: each vertex lies ON its two chord lines

assertions.name: vertex_strict_min_gap
assertions.detail: each vertex lies STRICTLY inside the third half-plane

assertions.name: vertex_gap_matches_2Rsinsin
assertions.detail: the gap equals the predicted 2 R sin sin (Lean: cos_sub_cos_two_mul_add, inscribedTriangle_vertex_incidence)

assertions.name: tiling_points_tested
assertions.detail: interior points, off the edge and chord lines

verdict: Every ingredient of the H4-5c-ii(b) tiling proof checks. The subset direction is a single positive-coefficient linear identity in both orientations; the covering direction follows from one sign relation whose positive coefficients forbid the two sign patterns that would leave a triangle point in no sector; the three circle points sit on the chord lines in the incidence pattern that pins the half-plane definition to the intended triangle, with the predicted 2 R sin sin gap; and the two memberships agree at the SET level off the null lines. All of these are now PROVED in Lean (OrthoschemeTiling.lean, sorry-free), so this is a regression check on the transcription rather than evidence for an open claim.
notes: No free parameter; nothing fitted; touches no production. Deterministic rational parameter grids -- no RNG and no float64 literals. R = 13/10 != 1 and t = 7/10 != 0 so that a spurious R-dependence or a dropped rotation would surface. No q0 anywhere: pure hyperbolic geometry, so the muon/proton anchor question does not arise.
